lead.text: Rabot Energy has raised $50m to turn a few hundred thousand German homes into one power station. The Hamburg company sells dynamic electricity tariffs, the kind that move a household's consumption into the cheaper and greener hours of the day, and it is now pooling the batteries sitting behind those meters into a virtual power plant that can be dispatched as a single unit. Endeit led the Series B with the DeepTech & Climate Fonds, and HV Capital, High-Tech Gründerfonds, Bosch Ventures, CNI, Acurio Ventures and vent.io all followed on. Chief executive Jan Rabe is assembling a power station out of appliances people bought for their own reasons.

source.title: Rabot Energy secures $50M to transform homes into a virtual power plant

lead.text: Ubitium has raised $14m for a chip that does all of it. A robot or a drone today carries a DSP for the sensors, an NPU for the model and a CPU for the control loop, and Ubitium builds one reconfigurable processor meant to do the three jobs on a single architecture. Ibex Investors led the seed round, with OpenOcean, the KBC Focus Fund, Runa Capital and Inflection following on. Florian Seibel, co-founder of Quantum Systems, put money in personally, which makes this a German chip company part-funded by the founder of a German drone company. That is roughly what rebuilding an industrial base looks like from the inside.

source.title: Ubitium raises $14M to bring universal computing to physical AI
